Clean Body Weight Records and Check Each Pig

Source: R/clean_weight.R
clean_weight.Rd

Flag implausible and outlying body weight records, then decide for each pig whether its weight data are good enough for growth analysis.

clean_weight(visits, qc = qc_config(), verbose = 1, cores = 1)

Arguments

visits

Visit table from prep_visits().

qc

QC settings from qc_config(). Used here: weight_range, adapt_days, weight_track, track_tol, weight_outlier, outlier_combine, rlm_cutoff, sd_max, loess_span, min_records, min_test_days, max_missing_rate, entry_weight_max, exit_weight_min, track_flag_share, smooth_r2_min.

verbose

0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details).

cores

Number of CPU cores for the per-pig computations. Default 1.

Value

An object of class ppt_weight (a list):

  • per_pig: one row per pig with n_records, n_valid, n_outliers, first_date, last_date, test_days, missing_rate, entry_weight, exit_weight (kg, from the LOESS smooth of the valid weights), r2 (R² of that smooth), track_removed (share of the records removed by the tracking, NA when not tracked), longest_gap_days (longest time without a visit), weight_jump_kg (from prep_visits(), NA without station transfer), status ("keep", "low_confidence" or "removed") and reason;

  • daily: one row per pig and day for pigs not removed: median of the valid weights (weight, kg), n_records, n_outliers;

  • records: every weight record with fitted, outlier and qc_flag (why it was flagged; "track" for records removed by the tracking);

  • removed: pigs removed here, plus misreads logged by prep_visits();

  • settings: the QC settings used.

Details

Pig checks use the valid (non-outlier) records only:

  • n_valid < min_records, test_days < min_test_days or missing_rate > max_missing_rate (share of test days without a valid weight) remove the pig;

  • entry_weight > entry_weight_max, exit_weight < exit_weight_min, a tracking that removes more than track_flag_share of the records, or r2 < smooth_r2_min mark the pig "low_confidence" but keep it: its growth can still be estimated by extrapolation in calc_adg(), with a flag;

  • so do a test interrupted for more than max_gap_days days (no visit at all, e.g. isolation for treatment: growth and intake around it are often not typical of the pig) and a body weight jump above max_jump_kg at a station transfer.

See also

prep_visits() for the previous step, qc_config() for the settings.

Examples

visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits)
#> 
#> ── Cleaning body weight (track + rlm + loess) ──────────────────────────────────
#>   Weight records                       31,472
#>   └ adaptation after entry (not used)   3,404   10.8%
#>   └ outliers                            5,667   18.0%
#>     └ by tracking                       1,543    4.9%
#> ! Pigs: 28 kept, 1 low confidence, 1 removed 0.6s
w
#> 
#> ── <ppt_weight> ──
#> 
#> Pigs: 30 (keep 28, low confidence 1, removed 1)
#> $per_pig: 30 rows x 17 columns
#> $daily: 2789 rows x 7 columns
#> $removed: 1 row x 4 columns
#> $records: 31472 rows x 10 columns

# Why pigs were removed
w$removed
#>    responder location         step               reason
#>       <char>   <char>       <char>               <char>
#> 1:     15964      101 clean_weight 0 valid weights < 20

# Records flagged as outliers
head(w$records[outlier == TRUE])
#>    responder location       date seq_days          entry_time weight fitted
#>       <char>   <char>     <Date>    <int>              <POSc>  <num>  <num>
#> 1:     13913      101 2024-02-19        1 2024-02-19 22:21:41   23.5     NA
#> 2:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 01:00:02   23.5     NA
#> 3:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 01:05:04   31.0     NA
#> 4:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 02:53:50   23.5     NA
#> 5:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 04:27:26   24.0     NA
#> 6:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 06:52:21   28.5     NA
#>    rlm_w outlier    qc_flag
#>    <num>  <lgcl>     <char>
#> 1:    NA    TRUE adaptation
#> 2:    NA    TRUE adaptation
#> 3:    NA    TRUE adaptation
#> 4:    NA    TRUE adaptation
#> 5:    NA    TRUE adaptation
#> 6:    NA    TRUE adaptation

# Other outlier methods
w_sd <- clean_weight(visits, qc = qc_config(weight_outlier = c("rlm", "sd")), verbose = 0)
table(w_sd$per_pig$status)
#> 
#>           keep low_confidence        removed 
#>             28              1              1
